```{python}
#| label: fig-bench-edge
#| fig-cap: "Edge cases: sparse get, deep get, drain"
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
ops = ['CS2 sparse\nget 10M', 'CoordSpaceN19 get\n100', 'Drain\n11,172']
cs_edge = [44.9, 7.04, 27.8]; hm_edge = [1050, 3.53, 20.0]; labels_edge = ['23.4x', '0.50x', '0.72x']
fig, ax = plt.subplots(); x = np.arange(len(ops)); w = 0.3
ax.bar(x - w/2, cs_edge, w, label='CoordSpace', color='white', edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.8, hatch='///')
ax.bar(x + w/2, hm_edge, w, label='HashMap', color='white', edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.8)
ax.set_xticks(x); ax.set_xticklabels(ops, fontsize=7); ax.set_ylabel('Latency (µs)')
ax.set_yscale('log'); ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc='upper left')
for i, (cs, hm, label) in enumerate(zip(cs_edge, hm_edge, labels_edge)):
    mid = (cs * hm) ** 0.5 if cs > 0 and hm > 0 else max(cs, hm)
    color = 'black' if 'x' in label else 'gray'
    ax.annotate(label, xy=(i, mid), fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.12', facecolor='white', edgecolor=color, alpha=0.85))
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```
